hypothesis: If a hive-bee comb cell is a hexagonal prism closed by three rhombic facets of a rhombic dodecahedron, then in 3-D measurements of bee-built cell bases (not foundation-formed bases) the three basal facets must be planar rhombi meeting pairwise at dihedral angles close to 120 degrees, with each rhombus having obtuse angles close to 109 degrees 28 minutes (arccos(-1/3)) and acute angles close to 70 degrees 32 minutes.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. From a public micro-CT or 3-D scan of natural (foundationless) worker comb, fit planes to the three basal facets of each measurable cell and compute the rhombus obtuse angle at the apex of the base. The claim is supported if the median apex angle over >= 20 cells lies within 109.47 +/- 3 degrees and the facet-plane fit residuals are small relative to wall thickness (planar facets), with the prismatic walls meeting at 120 +/- 5 degrees in cross-section.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. Refuted if the median apex angle differs from 109.47 degrees by more than 6 degrees (e.g. if bases are rounded or formed of a single curved surface with no three-facet structure in the majority of cells), or if fewer than half of the cells show three identifiable planar basal facets. Results in between are 'mixed'. If no public 3-D data of bee-built cell bases can be obtained, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable.
interpretation: Thompson's claim has two parts: a geometric description of the cell (hexagonal prism, three rhombic basal facets meeting at the tetrahedral angle 109 deg 28 min) and a minimal-surface rationale. Only the geometric description is tested here; the minimal-surface statement is a theorem about the rhombic dodecahedron (and is in fact not the true minimum, as Toth 1964 showed), not an empirical matter. The test requires 3-D geometry of bee-built cell bases. The two Dryad datasets listed were identified as the only public comb datasets found on Dryad, Zenodo and figshare on 2026-10-31; their README files were read to determine whether they contain basal-facet geometry before any data were downloaded.
